Customer Intelligence–Enabled Service Resolution Status: proposal. A controlled employee-assist pilot for one customer-service journey and one team. Intended outcome Help the servicing employee understand what happened, verify the current state of a customer issue and identify the next permitted step. The proposed workspace brings together relevant contacts, case history, authoritative status and approved service guidance with links to the underlying evidence. The employee reviews the interpretation, owns the response and approves any operational action. AI-generated interpretations remain distinguishable from verified facts. Candidate journeys Journey Proposed scope Payment Issue Resolution One domestic retail-payment type with supported failed, pending or reversed states. Card Dispute Progress Support One dispute type and servicing queue, using authoritative stage, evidence and deadline information. Onboarding/KYC Progress Support One onboarding path using permitted service-state metadata and approved customer-facing explanations. Payment Issue Resolution is the initial candidate, subject to confirmation of ownership, source availability and case volume. The pilot would implement one selected journey. Proposed delivery approach Agree the service problem, eligible cases, exclusions, ownership and measurement approach. Establish a baseline and manually review representative historical cases. Assemble a source-linked customer and case context with explicit freshness and access limits. Evaluate interpretation and proposed next steps against protected acceptance cases. Introduce controlled employee use only when the required readiness and approval conditions are met. Assess outcomes and decide whether to extend, refine or close the pilot. Compare the existing process, a context-only workspace and an AI-assisted workspace. This makes the additional contribution of AI visible alongside the value of better information access. Boundaries The proposal excludes autonomous customer communication, movement or reversal of funds, reimbursement decisions and regulated credit, fraud, AML, sanctions or onboarding decisions. Each journey has its own more restrictive data and action boundaries. Missing, conflicting or stale evidence leads to manual handling or specialist referral. The model does not establish authoritative banking facts or replace an unavailable source. Evidence and continuing ownership Evaluation covers source accuracy, permitted next steps, employee usefulness, repeat contact, handling effort, customer outcomes and control failures. Measures and thresholds are agreed for the selected journey after establishing the baseline. Before delivery is committed, the project needs named business and process owners, a measurement owner, confirmed source and interface owners, and arrangements for support, suspension and handover. Those appointments and commitments remain to be established.
